title: Model selector fallback contract: precedence, caching, and performance-profile binding
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
Define a deterministic, cross-environment contract for resolving model selectors supplied by API/SDK clients. Selectors include tag names (e.g., latest-stable), semver ranges (e.g., ^1.4.0), explicit semver (1.4.2), and immutable refs (commit hash or artifact id). The goal is to specify precedence, allowed fallbacks, caching semantics, and how published performance profiles bind to resolved versions so that hosted, dedicated, and private deployments behave predictably.
background: Current state: multiple teams have implemented ad-hoc pin semantics. SDK layer accepts a free-form string and runtime performs resolution. This leads to: inconsistent fallback behavior across Hosted vs Dedicated, stale client-side caches that point to retired builds, and ambiguity around which performance profile (latency/cost/seq-length profile) is authoritative for a given request. Recent customer incidents exposed regressions when model artifacts were retagged in the model catalog and SDKs did not surface the change clearly.
goals: Specify canonical selector grammar and precedence rules used by API, SDK, and runtime.
Define resolver contract for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) with clear fallback and error semantics.
Standardize caching and TTL semantics for selector resolution across SDKs and runtime nodes.
Define how performance profiles are published, versioned, and bound to model versions so routing decisions (e.g., kernel selection, KV sizing) are reproducible.
Provide migration and rollout plan that minimizes customer disruption.
Add tests, SDK examples, and docs for developers and support teams.
non_goals: Designing a new model registry UI (out of scope for this ticket).
Implementing on-prem packaging changes for Private beyond resolution behavior (will be separate).
design_decisions: 1) Selector precedence: explicit immutable refs (commit hash / artifact-id) > exact semver > semver ranges > named tags. 2) Tags are pointers and can be retagged; SDKs MUST treat tag resolution as potentially volatile and use short TTL caches by default. 3) Semver ranges resolve to the highest matching published release in the catalog at resolution time. 4) If resolution fails, runtime will optionally attempt a single compatible fallback according to a configurable policy (none | nearest-minor | pinned-fallback). 5) Performance profiles are first-class artifacts: each model artifact has an associated profile-id. Resolution returns both model-artifact-id and profile-id. Profile binding is immutable for the resolved artifact. 6) Private customers can opt into an offline resolution mode (catalog snapshot) for stricter stability guarantees.
tradeoffs:
- Strong immutability (commit hash-only) gives repeatability but poor UX for developers who expect tags like 'latest-stable' to float.
- Short TTL for tag caching reduces stale routing but increases catalog read pressure; mitigate with client-side jitter/backoff and runtime caching.
- Binding performance profiles at resolution time makes inference decisions reproducible but requires additional metadata storage and coordination when profiles are updated; we'll version profiles to avoid silent changes.
api_changes: Introduce a typed ModelSelector object in SDKs with fields: selector_type (string: 'tag'|'semver'|'range'|'ref'), selector_value (string), resolution_hint (optional: 'strict'|'best-effort'). Add 'resolved_model' field to generation API responses containing artifact_id, model_version, profile_id, and resolved_semver. Add optional query param 'snapshot=true' for Private deployments to request catalog snapshot resolution.
compatibility_notes:
- Old SDKs that pass free-form strings will continue to work via a compatibility shim for 6 months; however behavior will be logged as deprecated.
- Dedicated clusters with pinned catalogs must opt into a migration window to adopt semantic resolution semantics; we'll provide a migration tool to create catalog aliases mapping old pins to artifact IDs.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc merged to repo and reviewed by runtime, sdk, and onboarding teams.
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) implement ModelSelector and surface resolved_model metadata in responses.
Runtime resolver implements precedence and fallback policies and has unit+integration tests covering edge cases (tag retag, missing semver, conflicting tags).
Performance profile binding tests ensure the same resolved artifact yields identical kernel decisions in hosted and dedicated runs.
Docs and migration guide published; deprecation notice sent for legacy free-form selector usage.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Publish spec and compatibility shim; log deprecation warnings in SDKs and track usage metrics.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement resolver in runtime + profile binding; add SDK support to return resolved metadata; run canary on internal services.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Open beta for customers; provide migration tool to freeze catalog aliases.
Phase 4 (4 weeks): Default enforcement and deprecation removal for legacy selectors after customer outreach.
test_plan: Unit tests for selector parser across edge cases (invalid semver, range overlaps, malformed refs).
E2E tests: retag a tag to different artifact and ensure SDK TTL behavior is correct under different resolution_hints.
Load test: measure catalog resolution QPS with short TTLs and evaluate required cache sizes/backoffs.
Profile regression tests: define canonical prompts and assert latency/p99 changes within expected windows when profile upgrades occur.
rollout: Canary on internal infra -> 10% external Hosted traffic -> Dedicated opt-in -> Private snapshot mode rollout. Each stage must pass stability gates (error rate < 0.1%, no >3% latency regressions on control flows).
docs_tasks: Write SDK migration guide with examples for tag -> semver -> ref usage.
Add a FAQ about tag retagging and snapshot semantics for Private.
